concepts.title: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: The World as One Family

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: The World as One Family' refers to.
questions.a: The Hitopadesha verse that opens the chapter says the noble-minded count the whole world as one family, vasudhaiva kutumbakam; India has lived this ideal by welcoming peoples of many lands and faiths.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: The World as One Family'.
questions.a: Stranger-hood is a habit of small minds: India's civilisational habit has been to make newcomers its own.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: The World as One Family' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Communities that Made India Home' refers to.
questions.a: Over the centuries Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians, Muslims and others reached India's coasts and courts, fleeing persecution or seeking trade; each was allowed to worship, work and settle, and each enriched the land.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Communities that Made India Home'.
questions.a: Refugees became neighbours, and neighbours became Indians: acceptance turned arrival into belonging.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Communities that Made India Home' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Communities of settlers (source: gees205.txt, Communities of settlers)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Acceptance as an Indian Value' refers to.
questions.a: Acceptance is not mere tolerance: India's traditions taught that truth has many paths, so the newcomer's god, food and festival were given room beside one's own.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Acceptance as an Indian Value'.
questions.a: Tolerance merely permits; acceptance honours: the deeper value made India a home rather than a camp.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Acceptance as an Indian Value' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'How the Communities Enriched India' refers to.
questions.a: The communities that made India home gave generously: Parsi enterprise built industry, Syrian Christian and Jewish traditions enriched trade and letters, Islamic art and cuisine reshaped tastes, and all joined the common chorus of India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'How the Communities Enriched India'.
questions.a: Diversity is a treasury: every community that arrived left the country richer than it found it.

questions.q: Under which section is 'How the Communities Enriched India' taught, and from which source text?
